ChanServ INFO prints a channel's registration time with Go's time.RFC1123 layout, for example `Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 MST`.
ChanServ INFO, for operators with the chanreg capability, prints when a channel was purged with the time.RFC1123 layout.
Server-time message tags (IRCv3 server-time) use the layout `utils.IRCv3TimestampFormat`, `2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z`: RFC 3339 in UTC with milliseconds.

Services answer a command by `service.Notice(rb, text)`, which adds a NOTICE from the service to the requesting nick to the command's ResponseBuffer, so labeled-response clients get it under the command's label.

When ChanServ OPs someone, operators with the `channels` server-notice mask get a line such as `Client [nick!user@host] CS OP'd [target] in channel [#chan]` through `server.snomasks.Send(sno.LocalChannels, ...)`.
Registering a channel sends operators a `Channel registered [#chan] by [nick!user@host]` server notice on the LocalChannels mask.
NickServ reports a nickname enforcement setting as a plain NOTICE, `Your stored nickname enforcement setting is: <value>`, with no prefix naming the account.

Account settings (NickServ SET) are stored as one JSON value under the key `account.settings <casefolded account>`; a field added to AccountSettings needs no migration because a missing field decodes to its zero value.
Channel purge records are kept in their own datastore table, `datastore.TableChannelPurges`, separate from channel registrations.
A channel registration's dirty-bit flags are IncludeInitial, IncludeTopic, IncludeModes, IncludeLists and IncludeSettings; IncludeAllAttrs is all of them.
AMODEs (persistent channel modes for accounts) are saved in the registration as `AccountToUMode`, a map from account name to mode.
A channel's topic is saved in its registration with who set it (`TopicSetBy`) and when (`TopicSetTime`).
An empty channel is removed from memory unless it is registered: `Channel.IsClean` returns false for a registered channel.
CS TRANSFER to another account is pending until the recipient accepts (channelTransferPending), unless an operator forces it.
An account may register at most `channels.registration.max-channels-per-account` channels; when the key is missing or 0, LoadConfig sets it to 15; holders of the chanreg capability are exempt.
`default.yaml` is compiled into the binary with go:embed (ergo.go) and is what `ergo defaultconfig` prints; `traditional.yaml` is a second sample config kept beside it.
ChanServ handlers casefold a channel argument with `CasefoldChannel` before looking it up; INFO then prints the name from the registration (`chinfo.Name`).

A nickname registered to an account is reserved: connecting with it without logging in first gets 433 `Nickname is reserved by a different account` (and a FAIL NICK NICKNAME_RESERVED for clients with standard replies).
ChanServ LIST, which lists registered channels matching a regular expression, needs the chanreg operator capability.
For a user without the chanreg capability, ChanServ INFO on a purged channel says only that it was purged; the operator, the time and the reason are shown to chanreg holders.
Stored history older than `history.restrictions.expire-time` (default 1w) is not returned: GetHistorySequence computes the cutoff; operators with the history capability are exempt.
The SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL history back-ends each run a cleanupLoop that deletes rows older than the expire time; with expire-time 0 nothing is deleted.
CS SET offers three channel settings: history, query-cutoff and store-events, held in ChannelSettings in the registration.
NickServ SET keys are enforce, autoreplay-lines, replay-joins, multiclient, always-on, autoreplay-missed, auto-away, dm-history and email.
`make test` runs `python3 ./gencapdefs.py | diff - ./irc/caps/defs.go`, go test and go vet with the tags `i18n mysql postgresql sqlite` and again with none, then `./.check-gofmt.sh`.
ergo vendors every dependency (`vendor/`), so builds and tests need no `go get`; DEVELOPING.md advises against fetching modules.
Strings passed to `client.t()`, and most strings written in backticks, are picked up by `updatetranslations.py run irc languages` for translation through CrowdIn.
Help text in a services command table uses `$b` for bold, which ircfmt turns into IRC formatting.
`ergo genpasswd` reads a password twice and prints a bcrypt hash for an oper block's `password`.
`ergo initdb --conf <file>` creates the datastore at `datastore.path`; with `datastore.autoupgrade: true` an older schema is upgraded at start.
Operator capabilities come from oper-classes in the config; `chanreg` lets an operator modify any channel's registration.
In command handlers, replies go through the ResponseBuffer (`rb.Add*`), not `client.Send*`, so that labeled responses work.
Mutexes are tiered: while holding a tier-n mutex only strictly higher tiers may be taken; Channel.stateMutex is tier 1, ChannelManager's RWMutex tier 2, Server.rehashMutex tier 3.
The services command table field `authRequired: true` makes the service answer `You're not logged into an account` to users who are not logged in.
`minParams` in a services command table is the fewest parameters a command accepts; with fewer the service answers `Invalid parameters. For usage, do /msg <service> HELP <COMMAND>`.
Email to users (verification, password reset) is configured and sent by the `irc/email` package (MailtoConfig, with DKIM signing in dkim.go).
Server-notice masks such as LocalChannels and LocalOpers are defined in `irc/sno`; services send to them with `server.snomasks.Send`.
WHOWAS keeps a fixed-size list of recent nicks (`server.whoWas`), sized by `limits.whowas-entries` (100 in default.yaml).
The `irctest` submodule is the integration suite; `make irctest` installs ergo and runs it against the ergo on $PATH.
ChanServ PURGE (operators) blocks a channel name from use and records the operator, time and reason in a ChannelPurgeRecord.
`email.ComposeMail` writes only the From, To, Message-ID, Date and Subject headers and then the blank line that ends them; any other header (and the body) is the caller's to add.
`email.SendMail` checks the recipient against the address blacklist first and returns `ErrBlacklistedAddress` without connecting anywhere.

With `mta.server` set, `email.SendMail` connects to `server:port` of the configured smarthost; with none it looks up the MX record of the recipient's domain and sends directly (`DirectSendingEnabled`).
`MailtoConfig.DirectSendingEnabled` is true exactly when `mta.server` is empty.

`smtp.SendMail` opens one connection per message: it dials, says HELO, starts TLS if the server offers it (and requires it when `require-tls` is set), authenticates if given credentials, sends, and closes the connection when it returns.
An SMTP reply with an error code is returned by the `irc/smtp` client as a `*textproto.Error` carrying the code and the message, so a caller can tell a 4xx from a 5xx.
`email-verification.require-tls` is `true` in `default.yaml`, so a mail relay without STARTTLS refuses mail from a stock configuration until it is set to false.
`MailtoConfig.Postprocess` (default HELO domain, default protocol `tcp`, blacklist compilation) is called from `LoadConfig` only for an enabled `accounts.registration.email-verification` section.
The account-verification mail is sent from the registration command itself (`dispatchMailtoCallback`): `email.SendMail` is called synchronously and a failure is only logged and returned.
When a registration mail cannot be sent, the registration answers `Could not dispatch registration e-mail`.
`nsSetHandler` sends an unprivileged `NS SET EMAIL` to `nsSetEmailHandler`, which needs a confirmation, while the privileged SASET path changes the setting directly.
An account's email address is stored in the `Email` field of `AccountSettings`, in the same JSON value as its other NickServ settings.
NickServ SAREGISTER, which needs the `accreg` operator capability, registers an account on someone else's behalf; its table entry carries `capabs: accreg`.
NickServ SASET modifies another user's account settings for operators with `accreg`; its entry reuses `nsSetHandler`.
The unprivileged `NS SET EMAIL` only works when email verification is enabled, and sends a code to the new address before it takes effect.

`SnoManager.Send` returns at once when no client has the mask, and otherwise prefixes the text with the mask's name in grey (for example `CHANNEL`) before sending it as a NOTICE to every subscribed client.
The channels server-notice mask is the letter `j` (`sno.LocalChannels`, named CHANNEL) and the opers mask is `o` (`sno.LocalOpers`, named OPER).
`SnoManager.AddMasks` subscribes a client to the given server-notice masks; a client holds the masks it has chosen with `MODE <nick> +s`.
`ircService.Notice(rb, text)` adds the NOTICE to the ResponseBuffer of the command being answered, addressed to that buffer's target, the client that typed the command.
`Client.Send(tags, prefix, command, params...)` sends a message straight to every session of that client, not through any ResponseBuffer.
`Client.Notice(text)` sends a NOTICE from the server's own name to the client, outside any ResponseBuffer.
`DefaultMaxLineLen` is 512, the longest line, in bytes, the server reads from or writes to a client unless `server.max-line-len` raises it.
`LoadConfig` raises `server.max-line-len` to 512 when it is set lower.
The server writes each outgoing message with `LineBytesStrict(false, MaxLineLen)`, so a message's line is bounded by `MaxLineLen` bytes including its prefix and the trailing CRLF.
`AccountManager.Unregister` unregisters all of the account's channels in a deferred function, after the account's own data has been deleted.
`ChannelManager.ChannelsForAccount` lists the registered channels whose founder is the given (casefolded) account, leaving out secret channels unless asked for privileged results.
`AccountManager.AccountToClients` returns the clients currently logged into an account, looked up by its casefolded name.
`Channel.Transfer` completes at once when the caller is an operator with the chanreg capability (`hasPrivs`); otherwise the recipient has to accept it.
`CS UNREGISTER` asks for a confirmation code (`utils.ConfirmationCode` of the channel's name and registration time) before it unregisters a channel.
`NS UNREGISTER` asks for a confirmation code too, and an account can be unregistered by itself or by an operator with `accreg`.
In `Channel.Join`, joiners with no privileges are checked in this order: user limit (+l), key (+k), invite-only (+i), ban list (+b), registered-only (+R).
SAJOIN, the channel's founder, anyone who gets halfop or higher from an AMODE, and invited users skip the join restrictions in `Channel.Join` (`hasPrivs`).
In `joinHandler`, a join that fails with `errLimitExceeded` is answered with the numeric `ERR_CHANNELISFULL` (471), naming mode `l` as the restriction.
`Channel.SetRegistered` records the founder and the registration time, and makes the founder's persistent mode `ChannelFounder`; it fails if the channel is already registered.
`Channel.SetUnregistered` clears the founder, the registration time and the account modes, and gives the channel a new UUID so that a later registration is stored under a different datastore key.
`Channel.MarkDirty` records which parts of the registration changed and wakes the channel's writer only if the channel is registered.

A registered channel's writer goroutine (`writeLoop`) stores the registration, and writes again only if more changes were marked dirty meanwhile; it stops when nothing is dirty, and cleans the channel up if it is empty.
`ChannelManager.SetUnregistered` deletes the channel's row from the datastore, under the UUID the channel had, in a deferred call that runs after the channel itself has been reset.
At start-up `ChannelManager.loadRegisteredChannels` reads every registration from the datastore and builds an in-memory `Channel` for each one that is not purged.
`Channel.Purge` kicks everyone from the channel (it empties the member lists) and does not unregister it: its body never calls `SetUnregistered`.
`ChannelManager.Channels` returns every channel the server has in memory, registered or not, so callers that want registered ones check `IsRegistered`.
Time periods in the configuration that use `custime.Duration` accept days, months and years as well as Go's units (for example `1d`); the parser is a fork of `time.ParseDuration`.
`LoadConfig` fills defaults after parsing: for example `channels.max-channels-per-client` becomes 100 when it is 0 or missing.
`Server.Config()` returns the current `*Config` with an atomic load; a rehash stores a whole new `Config`, so the one a caller holds is a snapshot.
Periodic jobs in `server.go` re-arm themselves: the job does its work and ends with `time.AfterFunc(interval, server.periodic...)`.
`traditional.yaml` carries its own `channels.registration` section next to default.yaml's; a key added to one is not added to the other automatically.
`default.yaml` has `channels.registration.max-channels-per-account: 15` under `channels.registration`, together with `enabled` and `operator-only`.
`CS LIST` loops over `server.channels.AllRegisteredChannels()` and prints each matching channel's name, indented, to the requester.
`CS SET` looks the channel up with `server.channels.Get` and answers `No such channel` for an unknown one before it checks the setting.
The persistent state of a registered channel is one `RegisteredChannel` value, serialized to JSON with `json.Marshal` by `Serialize`.
`ChannelManager.Get` finds a channel by any name that casefolds the same, and returns nil when the server has no such channel in memory.

`Client.HasRoleCapabs("chanreg")` is how a handler asks whether the client is an operator with the chanreg capability; `capabs: []string{"chanreg"}` in a command's table entry makes ChanServ refuse everyone else.
`Channel.Members()` returns the channel's cached member slice (`membersCache`) under the read lock, so a caller can walk it without holding the lock and must not modify it.

`Channel.Join` is called with the joiner's ResponseBuffer and flushes it itself (`rb.Flush(true)`) after the JOIN, topic and names have been added, so anything added after that point is sent with the next flush.
`ChanServ`'s services prefix is `ChanServ!ChanServ@localhost` unless a services hostname is configured; unsolicited service messages take this as their prefix.
